etymologies.etymologyHTML: From X +‎ ray, a calque of German X-Strahl, coined by Wilhelm Röntgen upon his discovery of the rays in 1895, X signifying their unknown nature.

definitions.definition: (transitive, informal) To take a radiograph of; to obtain an image of using X-ray radiation, especially for the purpose of medical diagnostic evaluation.

quote.citation: 1925, Sidney Coe Howard, They Knew What They Wanted (Doubleday, Page and Company), Act II, page 116.
quote.text: Both legs broken in the morning. Tibia, fibula, femur, and ischium. X-rayed and set inside of an hour after the accident.

definitions.definition: Of or having to do with X-rays.

quote.citation: 1974, Shel Silverstein, “Who”, in Where the Sidewalk Ends, HarperCollins:
quote.text: Who will fly and have X-ray eyes— And be known as the man no bullet can kill?
